input_messages.content: Hello! I'm having trouble sending MMS messages from my phone for the past few hours. I would really like to fix this so I can send pictures to my family. Can you help me with that?
My name is John Smith, and my phone number is 555-123-2002. How can I verify my date of birth if you need it?
I don't want to change my plan. I think I would like to refuel some data. Can you please tell me how much data I should add to fix the MMS issue? Will 1 GB be enough?
Yes, please go ahead and refuel 1 GB for me. Thank you.
I confirmed that I want to refuel 1 GB for $2.00. Please proceed with that.
I confirmed that I want to refuel 1 GB for $2.00. Please proceed with that. Also, just to let you know, my phone's Data Saver mode is currently off.
Okay, I will try sending an MMS message now. Please hold on a moment.
I tried sending an MMS message, but it still doesn't work. What should I do next? I'm getting a bit frustrated with this.

I ran the checks you asked for. It says my phone is in Airplane Mode, the SIM card is missing, and there is no cellular or Wi-Fi connection. Mobile data and data roaming are off. The speed test also failed because there is no connection. What should I do now? I'm worried about the SIM card being missing.

I turned off Airplane Mode, and now the status bar shows no signal and data is disabled. Then I reseated the SIM card, and it says the SIM card is active and working, but the signal is poor and it's on 2G with data still disabled. What should I do next?

I turned mobile data on, but the status bar still showed poor signal and 2G. Then I checked the network mode preference, and it was set to 2G only. I changed it to 4G/5G preferred, and now the status bar shows excellent signal, 5G, and data enabled. What should I do next?
I ran the speed test, but it still failed with no connection. And my messaging app still cannot send MMS messages. What should I do next? I'm feeling a bit overwhelmed with all these steps.

The APN name on my phone is "internet," but the MMSC URL for picture messages is not set. Also, the VPN is turned off. What should I do next? I'm worried about rebooting my phone because I don't want to lose any photos.

I reset the APN settings and rebooted my phone. After reboot, the status bar still shows excellent signal, 5G, and data enabled. But the speed test failed again with no connection, and my messaging app still cannot send MMS messages. What should I do now? I'm really frustrated with this.

Here is what I found from the checks:

- Airplane mode is off, mobile data is on, and data roaming is off. The cellular connection is active with excellent 5G signal.
- The APN name is "internet" and the MMSC URL is now set to "http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc".
- Wi-Fi Calling is turned on.
- The messaging app has permission for phone, but I don't see storage or SMS permissions listed.

What should I do next?

I turned off Wi-Fi Calling and granted the messaging app permissions for storage and SMS. But my messaging app still cannot send MMS messages, and the speed test failed with no connection. I also tried sending a picture message, but it didn't work. What else can we try? I'm really hoping to get this fixed soon.

After rebooting, the status bar still shows excellent signal, 5G, and data enabled. But the speed test failed again with no connection, and my messaging app still cannot send MMS messages. It seems the problem is not fixed yet. Could you please transfer me to a human agent for further help? I would appreciate that.

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.
